title: Function-call behavior mapping and lossiness mitigation plan for Responses parity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Investigate and implement a translation layer and test harness that maps OpenAI Responses API function-calling semantics, streaming events, and structured-output conventions to Redwood's internal runtime semantics. Produce a runbook that quantifies types of lossy translations, defines mitigations and fallback behaviors, and implements canary scenarios to validate parity across typical customer workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A mapping document exists that lists every OpenAI Responses function-calling signal and its Redwood runtime equivalent (or explicit 'no equivalent') with lossiness tags.

A lightweight translation interceptor in the runtime can convert incoming Responses-style function call requests to Redwood's internal call representation with <15ms average overhead at p50 on canary nodes.
Canary test harness exercises streaming function call handshakes, mid-stream tool call interruptions, and structured output edge cases with automated pass/fail metrics.
Documentation and SDK change notes generated for downstream SDK teams showing behavioral deltas and recommended client-side patterns.
A fallback policy is implemented that will surface a clear error and optional migration hint when an irreversible semantic gap is detected at runtime.
Monitoring dashboards show lossiness rate and error classifications; alert thresholds added for >0.5% customer-impacting degradation in canary traffic.
technical_notes: Early discovery shows three classes of incompatibilities: 1) streaming framing differences (chunk vs event), 2) function-call lifecycle mismatches (pre-emit vs post-emit args finalization), and 3) structured output typing (OpenAI may attach inferred types to tool outputs). Proposed mitigation: implement a translation adapter layer with explicit event normalization, a strict function-call lifecycle state machine, and a lossiness metadata header appended to responses for telemetry. Runtime interceptor should be feature-flag gated and staffed on dedicated canary nodes before global rollout.
tasks: Draft exhaustive mapping table (OpenAI event -> Redwood event) and lossiness scoring rubric
Implement translation adapter prototype in runtime (node-level interceptor)
Create unit + integration tests to simulate mid-stream tool call preemption and argument mutation
Build canary harness: replay recorded OpenAI-style traffic and validate Redwood responses against an oracle
Add telemetry keys: translation_kind, lossiness_score, unmatched_fields
Document migration guidance and SDK snippets for Node/Python/Go
Run 48h canary, collect metrics, iterate on adapter performance
Prepare RFC for rollout with rollback and SLA impact assessment
